stories.title: Understand competitor landscape for EscapePlan
stories.story: As an owner operator, I want a clear competitor matrix so that we can position EscapePlan around offline reliability and mobile capabilities.
acceptanceCriteria: Feature comparison for OffTheCouch, Houdini MC, Escape Room Master, Escape Room Admin, and ClueMaster is documented.
Differentiators for offline-first Pi deployments are listed.
Risks from parity gaps captured in risk register.
stories.businessValue: Ensures the roadmap emphasizes competitive advantages for store and mobile operations; informs MVP focus.
stories.technicalNotes: project-docs/project-overview.md §1.1.1 holds matrix; sync with TODO risk register RISK-002.
risks: Missing competitor insights leads to scope creep later.
testCases: Review project-docs/project-overview.md and confirm competitor matrix exists.

stories.title: Lock MVP scope and success metrics
stories.story: As an owner operator, I need the MVP boundaries defined so that we can deliver a focused release quickly.
acceptanceCriteria: MVP feature list split between store-front and mobile operations is documented.
Success metrics (uptime, setup time, operator clicks) appear in overview section 1.5.
Out-of-scope backlog created for future releases.
stories.businessValue: Prevents scope drift and aligns pilot expectations.
stories.technicalNotes: Update roadmap in section 17 with v0.2+ candidates.
testCases: Validate overview document contains success metrics table.
Verify project-docs/project-overview.md §1.4 and §17 describe MVP scope and roadmap with store/mobile split.

stories.title: Document hardware and network baseline
stories.story: As the platform lead, I want a hardware/network baseline so the base image meets performance needs.
acceptanceCriteria: Pi performance envelope and camera capacity are listed.
AC600M configuration parameters recorded.
Peripheral checklist created for store and mobile kits.
stories.businessValue: Guides pi-gen configuration and procurement planning.
stories.technicalNotes: Include thermal considerations and power budgets.
testCases: Check architecture docs for hardware baseline appendix.

stories.title: Clarify domain model and service boundaries
stories.story: As the backend lead, I need domain context diagrams so that services remain modular.
acceptanceCriteria: Domain model covers users, games, rooms, bookings, sessions, hints, cameras, mobile kits.
Context diagrams highlight interactions between API, streaming, scheduling, and reporting modules.
Artifacts stored in project-docs/architecture/.
stories.businessValue: Reduces rework during API implementation.
stories.technicalNotes: Better Auth (Fastify + Drizzle + SvelteKit cookies) provides session management and username login across API and console.
testCases: Open architecture diagrams and confirm coverage of all core entities.

stories.title: Define UX strategy and DaisyUI theme
stories.story: As the frontend lead, I need a documented design system so the PWA feels cohesive on mobile devices.
acceptanceCriteria: Custom DaisyUI theme tokens defined with target palette.
Responsive layout guidelines documented for phone and tablet viewports.
Accessibility checklist created (WCAG AA targets).
stories.businessValue: Accelerates UI build and ensures accessibility from day one.
stories.technicalNotes: Better Auth (Fastify + Drizzle + SvelteKit cookies) provides session management and username login across API and console.
testCases: Inspect design docs for DaisyUI theme configuration.

stories.title: Build escapeplan-base pi-gen image
stories.story: As the platform lead, I want a reproducible base image so deployment to Pi is turnkey.
acceptanceCriteria: pi-gen repo builds image containing Node.js 22, ffmpeg, and nginx.
Automated build:image script documented and passing.
Image boots to configured EscapePlan services baseline.
stories.businessValue: Guarantees consistent field deployments and simplifies support.
stories.technicalNotes: 2025-09-29: pi-gen Stage 2 overlay installs Node 22, network services, systemd units, and packaging/health scripts; image build pending qemu-user-static on host. Image artifact 2025-09-30-escapeplan-os-lite.img generated and recorded in artifacts/ with manifest + sha256.
testCases: Execute pnpm run build:image and verify success on arm64 runner.

stories.title: Automate Wi-Fi AP and DHCP for EscapePlan
stories.story: As the platform lead, I need the Pi to broadcast a reliable private network so operators can connect anywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: hostapd/dnsmasq configs generated from templates with EscapePlan SSID.
Services auto-start on boot and recover after power loss.
Channel plan documented for crowded events.
stories.businessValue: Ensures offline independence without manual setup.
testCases: Boot image and confirm SSID broadcast + DHCP lease assignment.

stories.title: Keep services resilient and observable
stories.story: As the platform lead, I want managed systemd units and health checks so downtime is minimized.
acceptanceCriteria: escapeplan-api and escapeplan-ffmpeg@ units restart on failure with logging.
Health endpoints expose service state and disk usage.
Runbook documents restart and troubleshooting steps.
stories.businessValue: Supports reliable game-day operations without engineering support.
testCases: Simulate service crash and confirm auto-restart and alert logging.

stories.title: Secure system and ensure recoverability
stories.story: As the platform lead, I need security hardening and backups so data is safe even offline.
acceptanceCriteria: Firewall, SSH policy, and user accounts defined.
Automated database and asset backups scheduled with retention.
OTA/rollback process documented for operators.
stories.businessValue: Protects customer data and reduces recovery time after incidents.
testCases: Run backup job and restore on test Pi.

stories.title: Establish database migrations and seed data
stories.story: As the backend lead, I need schema migrations and real seed data so the system boots with meaningful records.
acceptanceCriteria: Drizzle migrations cover all MVP tables with constraints.
Seed scripts populate roles, games, rooms, pricing, and mobile kit templates.
Migrations run idempotently during CI and device provisioning.
stories.businessValue: Prevents mock data reliance and accelerates QA.
stories.technicalNotes: Initial migration scaffolding added; schema mirrored in seed but lint fixes pending before enabling automated migrations. Rollup/esbuild binaries must be reinstalled on current host before CI verifies seeds.
testCases: Run migration + seed on clean SQLite DB and verify data counts.

stories.title: Provide secure authentication and RBAC
stories.story: As a general manager, I need role-based access so staff only see what they need.
acceptanceCriteria: Admins manage users and reset passwords locally.
Session cookies expire appropriately with secure flags.
RBAC guards protect admin settings and bookings.
stories.businessValue: Protects operations while keeping workflow efficient.
stories.technicalNotes: Better Auth (Fastify + Drizzle + SvelteKit cookies) provides session management and username login across API and console.
testCases: Attempt unauthorized access and confirm denial across roles.
notes: 2025-09-29: Better Auth with username + admin plugins now replaces bespoke bearer tokens; Drizzle adapter persists sessions in SQLite.
2025-09-29: Admin console consumes Better Auth cookies and session middleware; login/logout flows wired through provider actions.
2025-09-29: Console supports self-service profile edits (name/email/bio/avatar) while admin management forms capture the new fields.
2025-09-29: Backend seed auto-runs in tests, generating admin credentials through Better Auth before exercising protected routes.
2025-09-30: Follow-up UI polish (modal-driven create/edit, confirmation dialogs, archive workflows) tracked in P3-013.

stories.title: Manage games, puzzles, and hints
stories.story: As a content designer, I want to curate puzzles and hints so each game stays up to date.
acceptanceCriteria: CRUD operations for games, rooms, puzzles, hints with media upload.
Hints ordered and categorized for quick access during sessions, supporting text, image, audio, and video formats.
Set room screen background asset and theme tokens per game, with audit log entries.
stories.businessValue: Keeps experiences fresh and ensures hints are operator-ready.
stories.technicalNotes: Table/list UI and modal-driven game editor pending (P3-014) to replace current inline forms; ensure backend contracts document every field.
testCases: Create new puzzle with hints and confirm availability in game runner.

stories.title: Schedule bookings for store and mobile events
stories.story: As a general manager, I need unified booking tools so I can avoid conflicts across rooms and mobile events.
acceptanceCriteria: Bookings capture party size, pricing tiers, deposit amount, and discount code.
System prevents double-booking of rooms or simultaneous sessions for the same game.
Provide daily calendar and printable schedule filtered by storefront vs mobile flag.
stories.businessValue: Maximizes utilization and prevents on-site conflicts.
stories.technicalNotes: Bookings manifest wired to stores with print action; offline queue + export still need live data stream. Vite dev server currently blocked by missing Rollup binary until node_modules are rebuilt locally.
testCases: Create overlapping bookings and verify conflict warning.

stories.title: Control sessions with real-time timers and hints
stories.story: As a game master, I need a responsive game runner so I can keep teams engaged and track hints.
acceptanceCriteria: Start/pause/resume timers with <500ms latency on updates.
Send predefined or custom hints (text/image/audio/video) and log automatically.
Mark puzzles completed and view history per session; play audio cue when hint delivered.
stories.businessValue: Delivers smooth in-room experience and accurate records.
stories.technicalNotes: Runner UI hooked to realtime stores with offline queue; next iteration (P3-015) adds ad-hoc session launch, quick-add from dashboard, and static room slug links for in-room displays. Rollup reinstall required before we can test websocket ack path locally.
testCases: Run simulated session verifying timer resilience after refresh.

stories.title: Monitor cameras and stream health
stories.story: As the technician, I want to manage cameras so video tiles stay reliable.
acceptanceCriteria: Register cameras with encrypted credentials and assign to rooms.
See live status and restart failing streams from UI.
Receive alerts when streams drop frames or stall.
stories.businessValue: Maintains situational awareness without manual restarts.
testCases: Disable camera feed and verify alert plus auto-recovery.

stories.title: View operations dashboard
stories.story: As a general manager, I need a dashboard to see all active games, timers, and alerts at a glance.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard lists active sessions with timers and camera thumbnails.
Quick actions available without leaving dashboard.
Health banner indicates network/offline status.
stories.businessValue: Enables one operator to oversee multiple rooms efficiently.
testCases: Launch dashboard on tablet and confirm layout remains responsive.

stories.title: Provide game-specific timer view for players
stories.story: As a participant in the room, I want a branded timer display so I can track progress and receive hints visually.
acceptanceCriteria: Each game slug renders timer, hint notifications, and room background image/video.
Display updates in sync with operator actions with drift ≤1s.
Works offline within local network tablets without authentication.
stories.businessValue: Improves immersion and reduces need for separate timer hardware.
stories.technicalNotes: Timer slug page subscribes to websocket updates with polling fallback; bundler issues need resolution before full offline package. Requires reinstalling Rollup native binary on current host.
testCases: Open slug page and verify timer matches operator console.

stories.title: Label mobile-ready games and assets
stories.story: As the owner, I want to flag which games are mobile-ready so I can schedule them for offsite events.
acceptanceCriteria: Games include an `is_mobile` flag visible in admin UI and APIs.
Bookings list mobile games separately with location notes and required transport instructions.
Reports can filter by mobile vs storefront bookings.
stories.businessValue: Keeps catalog organized for mobile deployments without full kit inventory.
testCases: Mark kit item missing and verify warning on upcoming event.

stories.title: Capture mobile booking logistics notes
stories.story: As the owner, I need to record logistics for mobile bookings so crews know where to go.
acceptanceCriteria: Bookings support free-form location notes, arrival window, and contact details.
System warns when mobile bookings overlap for the same game or crew but does not auto-route travel.
Printable run sheet includes mobile-specific notes.
stories.businessValue: Protects customer experience and reduces overtime.
stories.technicalNotes: Travel time calculations deferred; manual buffers only.
testCases: Schedule overlapping mobile events and ensure conflict detection triggers.

stories.title: Operate offline with reliable sync
stories.story: As the mobile coordinator, I need offline access and sync so events run even without internet.
acceptanceCriteria: Critical data (bookings, puzzles, hints) cached on devices prior to events.
Offline hint/session actions queue locally and sync when back online.
Operators see sync status and conflict prompts with manual resolution steps.
stories.businessValue: Enables revenue from remote events without connectivity costs.
testCases: Simulate offline session and confirm data syncs correctly after reconnection.

stories.title: Review analytics and daily run sheets
stories.story: As the owner, I want visibility into performance so I can plan staffing and marketing.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard shows throughput, hint usage, and revenue summaries derived from deposits/balances.
Exports available as CSV/PDF without internet access.
Reports differentiate store vs mobile bookings.
stories.businessValue: Supports data-driven decisions and future growth.
testCases: Generate daily report and confirm metrics accuracy against sample data.

stories.title: Receive alerts for operational issues
stories.story: As a general manager, I need local alerts when streams or timers fail so I can act immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: Alerts triggered for camera downtime, paused timers, and offline services.
Operators can acknowledge, mute, or escalate alerts.
Alerts logged for later review.
stories.businessValue: Reduces downtime and keeps games on schedule.
testCases: Force ffmpeg failure and confirm alert notifications appear.

stories.title: Pilot, test, and launch EscapePlan
stories.story: As the owner, I want a disciplined pilot and launch plan so the MVP is reliable from day one.
acceptanceCriteria: E2E tests automated across critical flows.
Load/performance tests documented with mitigation strategies.
Pilot feedback captured and release package assembled.
stories.businessValue: Ensures the MVP can be trusted in production environments.
testCases: Review pilot report and verify backlog updates created for feedback.

stories.title: Ensure EscapePlan appliances back up data and telemetry automatically
stories.story: As an operations lead, I need automated backups and scheduled maintenance tasks so that no session or auth data is lost if a Pi fails.
acceptanceCriteria: Nightly database and auth backups stored locally with export instructions.
Cron jobs documented for cleanup/log rotation.
Restore runbook validated on a fresh appliance.
stories.businessValue: Protects bookings and operational data during pilot incidents and simplifies disaster recovery.
stories.technicalNotes: Coordinate with Better-Auth/Better-Auth storage decision before finalizing backup scope.
risks: Backups consuming SD card space if retention not enforced.
testCases: Simulate nightly backup cron and verify archives exist.
Restore backup onto clean database and confirm operator login works.

stories.title: Streamline EscapePlan admin console workflows
stories.story: As a general manager, I want a polished admin console so I can manage users, games, and network settings quickly during live operations.
acceptanceCriteria: All admin forms provide inline validation and success/error feedback.
Role/permission visibility is clear for each navigation link.
PWA prompts and update banners behave consistently across browsers.
stories.businessValue: Reduces training time and minimizes operational mistakes during busy sessions.
stories.technicalNotes: Build on Better-Auth/Refine foundation once finalized; reuse DaisyUI theme tokens.
risks: Design churn if Better-Auth components differ from current layout.
testCases: Run usability walkthrough covering user creation, game edits, network updates.
Verify offline queue + PWA reload prompt flow after service worker update.

stories.title: Admin archives inactive operators
stories.story: As a general manager, I want to archive operators who no longer work here so that the user list stays clean without losing historical records.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin can click "Archive" button on any user card
System shows confirmation modal asking for archive reason (optional note)
After confirmation, user disappears from default list view
Archived users are blocked from login and API access
Admin can toggle "Show archived" filter to view archived users
Archived users can be unarchived with a single click (restores full access)
Hard delete option requires typing the username for safety
All archive actions are logged with timestamp, actor, and reason
stories.businessValue: Maintains clean operator lists for daily use while preserving audit trails and allowing reversible offboarding.
stories.technicalNotes: Archive adds archivedAt, archivedBy, archivedReason fields; blocks Better Auth sessions; unarchive clears these fields instantly.
testCases: Archive a user and verify they cannot log in.
Toggle "Show archived" and confirm archived users appear.
Unarchive a user and verify login works again.
Attempt hard delete without typing username and confirm prevention.
notes: 2025-10-01: Operator archive modal/list audited; functionality meets requirements but minor UX polish pending (toggle presentation, touch sizing).

stories.title: Manager edits game with intuitive tabbed interface
stories.story: As a content designer, I want to edit game details using a well-organized tabbed form so I can manage complex game configurations without feeling overwhelmed.
acceptanceCriteria: Manager clicks game name in list, modal opens with 6 tabs visible
Tab 1 (Game Details): Edit name, slug auto-updates but is overridable, set duration with minute picker, choose difficulty with star selector, add category tags, set player min/max with validation
Tab 2 (Images & Media): Upload game thumbnail with preview, upload room background for timer display, upload gallery images with drag-to-reorder, select theme token from dropdown
Tab 3 (Rooms): See list of rooms assigned to game, click "Add Room" to open nested form, each room shows name, UUID (read-only), description, mobile capability toggle, capacity number

Tab 4 (Puzzles & Hints): See collapsible puzzle cards with drag handles for reordering, click "Add Puzzle" for new puzzle form, expand puzzle to see nested hint list, add hints by type (text/image/audio/video), preview hints before saving
Tab 5 (Pricing): Select pricing model (per person or flat rate), add pricing tiers with category dropdown, set deposit requirements, add discount codes with expiration dates
Tab 6 (Booking Rules): Toggle if game is mobile-capable, if mobile: add location notes template and travel buffer, set reservation style (public/private), write cancellation policy text
On mobile: tabs are horizontal at top and swipeable, form is full-screen
On desktop: tabs are vertical on left side, form is centered modal with max 900px width
Form validates before allowing save: slug must be unique, min players cannot exceed max, at least one room/puzzle/hint/pricing tier required
Save button shows loading state while uploading assets and saving all tabs
Success message confirms save with option to close or continue editing
stories.businessValue: Dramatically improves content management UX by organizing complex game data into logical sections, reducing errors and time spent on game configuration.
stories.technicalNotes: Uses DaisyUI tabs component; mobile has top horizontal tabs (swipeable), desktop has side vertical tabs; asset uploads show progress bars; slug auto-generation uses lowercase + hyphens; UUIDs prevent FK breakage if names change.
testCases: Create game with all tabs filled and verify save success.
Attempt save with invalid data (slug duplicate, min > max players) and verify validation errors.
Test mobile viewport with swipeable tabs.
Upload assets and verify progress indicators work.
notes: 2025-10-01: Game modal now auto-generates slugs, exposes star difficulty selector, and supports drag/drop ordering with validation; asset management flows and comprehensive testing still pending.

stories.title: Game master quick-starts walk-in session
stories.story: As a game master, I want to quickly start a game for walk-in customers without creating a full booking so I can accommodate last-minute players efficiently.
acceptanceCriteria: Game master clicks "+ Quick Start" button on dashboard or game runner page

Modal opens with four fields visible: Game selector (dropdown with search), Room selector (filtered to available rooms), Party size (number with game min/max validation), Duration override (optional, defaults to game duration), Notes field (optional, for internal use)
Room selector only shows rooms that are currently available (no active session)
If attempting to select occupied room, tooltip shows "Room occupied until HH:MM"
Game master fills required fields and clicks "Start Session"
System creates synthetic booking with status "ADHOC", customer name "Walk-in", email blank
Session immediately starts in RUNNING state with countdown timer
Game master is redirected to full game runner page for that session
Dashboard updates in real-time showing new active session with "Ad-hoc" badge
Room timer display page automatically shows the new countdown (if TV is already tuned to that game's URL)
Session appears in "Active Sessions" widget with gray "Ad-hoc" label
All hint dispatch, timer controls, and session end flows work identically to booked sessions
stories.businessValue: Enables flexible operations for walk-in traffic without forcing staff to create fake customer bookings, improving response time and reducing friction.
stories.technicalNotes: Quick start uses same modal on dashboard and game runner; keyboard shortcut Cmd/Ctrl+K; validates room availability before allowing save; creates booking with is_adhoc=true, status='ADHOC'; redirects to /games/:sessionId after creation.
testCases: Launch quick start from dashboard, fill form, verify session starts.
Attempt to select occupied room and verify validation prevents selection.
Create ad-hoc session and verify "Ad-hoc" badge appears on dashboard.
Test keyboard shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+K) opens modal.
notes: 2025-10-01: Quick-start modal highlights occupied rooms, clamps party size, adds Cmd/Ctrl+K launcher, and redirects to runner; camera badges, deeper UX polish, and full functional validation remain.

stories.title: Admin configures and monitors network cameras
stories.story: As the technician, I want to add cameras to the system and assign them to rooms so operators can view live feeds during games without manual configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Technician navigates to Admin → Cameras page
Page shows list of cameras as cards on mobile, table on desktop
Each camera card shows: live thumbnail (5s refresh), name, room assignment, status badge (online/offline/testing), last seen timestamp if offline, action menu
Technician clicks "+ Add Camera" button in header

Modal opens with fields: Camera name (required), Room assignment (optional dropdown), Protocol (dropdown: RTSP/MJPEG/ONVIF), Host/IP (validated), Port (default 554 for RTSP), Username (optional), Password (optional, masked), Stream path (e.g. /stream)
Advanced settings (collapsible): Resolution dropdown (480p/720p/1080p/Native), Frame rate (FPS, default 15), Transport (TCP/UDP/HTTP)
Technician fills connection details and clicks "Test Connection" button
System attempts connection with 5-second timeout
If successful: preview window shows 5-second clip from camera, "Connection successful" message displays
If failed: error message shows specific issue ("Camera not responding", "Invalid credentials", "Stream format not supported") with diagnostic hints
Technician can save camera even if test fails (for debugging later)
After saving, camera appears in list with status badge
Technician can edit camera, click "Start Stream" to begin HLS pipeline
HLS status shows: Streaming (green with bitrate/fps), Stopped (gray), Error (red with error message)
Technician can drag-drop camera to different room in room assignment field
Credentials are stored encrypted, URLs display as rtsp://****:****@host/path
All connection attempts are logged for troubleshooting
stories.businessValue: Simplifies camera setup and troubleshooting by providing visual feedback and detailed diagnostics, reducing downtime and technical support burden.
stories.technicalNotes: Camera list refreshes thumbnails every 5s; test connection has 5s timeout; credentials encrypted with libsodium; HLS controls start/stop systemd ffmpeg@ workers; logs stored for diagnostics; status badges color-coded.
testCases: Add camera with valid credentials and verify test connection succeeds.
Add camera with invalid credentials and verify error message displays.
Start HLS stream and verify status changes to "Streaming".
Verify credentials display as masked in camera list.

stories.title: Admin monitors storage usage and manages assets
stories.story: As a general manager, I want to see how much storage is being used and by what so I can avoid running out of space and manage assets effectively.
acceptanceCriteria: Manager navigates to Admin → Storage page
Dashboard shows donut chart with three segments: Used (blue), Reserved (yellow), Available (green), center shows percentage used
Below chart, metric cards display: Total capacity, Used space, Available space, Number of assets, Largest single asset, Oldest backup date
Storage breakdown section shows: Database size, Assets total (with count by type: images/audio/video), HLS cache size, Backups total, Logs size, System (OS/packages)
Manager clicks "Asset Library" tab
Asset library shows grid view on desktop (4 columns), fewer on mobile (2 columns)
Toggle button switches to list view (table with columns: thumbnail, name, type, size, used by, uploaded date, actions)
Each asset card shows thumbnail or icon, filename, type badge (image/audio/video), size, "Used in X games" indicator

Manager clicks asset to open detail modal showing: full preview (image viewer/audio player/video player), metadata (filename, dimensions, duration, size, uploaded by/when), usage report listing which games/puzzles/hints use this asset
If asset is in use, delete button shows warning: "This asset is used in 3 hints. Delete anyway?"
Manager clicks "Upload" button, drag-drop zone appears
Manager drags multiple files, sees progress bar per file
System validates: images max 5MB, audio max 10MB, video max 50MB, rejects larger files with error message
System auto-converts images to WebP, videos to MP4 H.264 for compatibility
Manager clicks "Backups" tab
Backup list shows: timestamp, type (auto/manual), size, status (complete/in progress/failed), actions (download/restore/delete)
Manager clicks "Trigger Backup Now" button, backup job starts, progress indicator appears
Manager can download any backup as .tar.gz file
Manager can click "Restore" but system shows strong warning: "This will overwrite current database. Continue?"
Backup retention policy shown: "Keeping last 7 backups" with link to change settings
Manager clicks "Logs" tab
Log viewer shows: service selector (API/ffmpeg/nginx/systemd), date range picker, severity filter (error/warn/info/debug), live tail toggle
Logs display with syntax highlighting (errors in red, warnings in yellow)
Manager can download logs as .txt file or export full diagnostics bundle
stories.businessValue: Provides visibility into storage usage and asset management, preventing system failures due to full disks and enabling proactive maintenance.
stories.technicalNotes: Donut chart uses Chart.js or similar; asset library supports grid/list toggle; uploads show progress; backups downloaded as .tar.gz; logs use syntax highlighting; retention configurable (default 7 backups).
testCases: Navigate to Storage page and verify donut chart displays correctly.
Upload asset and verify it appears in asset library.
Delete asset in use and verify warning appears.
Trigger manual backup and verify it completes successfully.
View logs and verify filtering works correctly.

stories.title: Platform team aligns operator auth with Better-Auth schema
stories.story: As the lead developer, I need the operator database and auth flows to follow Better-Auth's canonical schema so that credentials, roles, and avatars remain consistent across the platform.
acceptanceCriteria: Operators table stores avatar_config as structured JSON that matches DiceBear Bottts options.
Create/update APIs rely solely on Better-Auth adapters for role, permission, and avatar persistence.
Automated tests cover create/update/archive flows using Better-Auth helpers and validate stored JSON.
Migration plan documented with rollback steps and references to Better-Auth documentation.
stories.businessValue: Ensures long-term maintainability and security by consolidating on a single auth provider schema.
stories.technicalNotes: Reference Better-Auth Drizzle adapter docs; coordinate with CLAUDE-2 on payload shapes.
risks: Incorrect migration could orphan existing sessions.
testCases: Create operator via API and confirm avatar_config JSON stored in database.
Update operator avatar and verify Better-Auth adapter returns updated image payload.
Archive operator and ensure session revocation continues to work.
notes: Assigned to CLAUDE-1. Must cross-check SESSION_6 plans and Better-Auth docs before implementation.

stories.title: Admin console honors Better-Auth-managed operator profiles
stories.story: As an operations manager, I want the admin console to load and save operator profiles through the Better-Auth-backed API so that avatars, roles, and permissions stay consistent without random resets.
acceptanceCriteria: Editing a user shows the persisted avatar and role data without reseeding.
Saving changes updates Better-Auth and the operators table, with confirmation in UI and API responses.
Automated UI tests cover create/edit/archive flows with avatar assertions.
QA report documents manual validation across Users, Roles, Permissions, Network, and Storage panels.
stories.businessValue: Keeps operator management trustworthy and prevents accidental credential drift.
stories.technicalNotes: Coordinate with CLAUDE-1 for payload schema; reference Better-Auth and SESSION_6 admin panel requirements.
risks: UI could desync if schema changes aren’t handled atomically.
testCases: Open edit modal for existing operator and confirm avatar matches stored config.
Randomize avatar, save, and verify API + UI reflect new config.
Regression test ensures archived operators remain blocked from login after UI edits.
notes: Assigned to CLAUDE-2. Provide QA artifacts for CLAUDE (QA) sign-off.

personas.description: Runs both the physical escape room venue and mobile event business.

personas.name: General Manager
personas.description: Coordinates daily operations, staffing, and customer experience across locations.

personas.name: Game Master
personas.description: Operates games in real time, orchestrating hints, timers, and customer interactions.

personas.name: Mobile Coordinator
personas.description: Plans and executes offsite escape room experiences using portable kits.

personas.name: Technician
personas.description: Maintains hardware, cameras, and network stability in store and mobile setups.

personas.name: Content Designer
personas.description: Designs puzzles and hint flows that operators execute.

personas.name: Customer (Participant)
personas.description: Players experiencing the game, either in-store or through mobile events.

Offline sync conflicts during mobile events
Crew scheduling gaps for mobile events

qualityGates.name: MVP Exit Criteria
criteria: All CRITICAL stories completed and tested
E2E tests pass on Raspberry Pi

priorityDefinitions.CRITICAL: Must be delivered for MVP viability.
priorityDefinitions.MEDIUM: Important but can slip to 0.1.x patch if needed.
